# Image Source and Sampling Boundary {#sec-boundary}

## Hospital storage to Workbench admission

![Image ownership and staging boundary. Source: `docs/adr/architecture/03-image-staging-boundary.mmd`.](../../adr/architecture/rendered/03-image-staging-boundary.png){#fig-boundary width=55%}

1. **Hospital-controlled storage** holds candidate images. It is outside the software.
2. **Authorized human selection.** A clinician or authorized hospital user chooses each image. The project team and the software never browse storage or pre-select images (owner decision, IMG-SAMP-001).
3. **Approved staging.** The hospital's own process copies the original file into the Workspace input folder.
4. **Workbench admission.** `scan_input_folder` reads **only that folder, top level only**. It skips symlinks and ancillary files (`.csv .json .md .txt .log .toml .xml .yaml .yml`), records SHA-256 identity, and applies conservative admission rules (@sec-admission).

There is no PACS query, storage crawler, or automatic patient selection anywhere in the code. Adding one would cross an owner-decided boundary and needs a new normative specification.

## Source class versus Workbench grade

::: {.callout-warning title="Safety -- two taxonomies, never merged"}
The source hospital's **`Refer` / `Not-refer`** class is **not** stored anywhere in the Workbench. The Workbench records a **clinician DR grade 0--4** (`reviewed_grade`, with `grade_review_source` = `AI_ACCEPTED` / `AI_CORRECTED` / `MANUAL`) and **annotations**. These are different taxonomies, produced at different times by different processes. Do not add code that derives one from the other.
:::

The team links the source class (and sex, where approved) to exported images outside the software. It joins its own record to `images.csv` by `image_id` or `image_sha256` (IMG-SAMP-013, IMG-SAMP-091). If the owner later wants the source class inside the Workbench, that is a contract change: it touches admission, the case schema, `DATASET_MANIFEST.md`, and the tests, and it needs a spec first.

## What the software contributes to coverage monitoring

| Coverage dimension | Held by the Workbench? | Export column |
|:-------------------|:-----------------------|:--------------|
| Refer / Not-refer | No | None; the team record holds it |
| Sex | No | None; the team record holds it |
| Laterality | Yes: clinician-confirmed in **Confirm Image** | `laterality`, `laterality_resolution_method` (`MANUAL` = confirmed) |
| Patient grouping | Yes: pseudonymous key | `patient_key`, `training_group_key` |
| Exact duplicates | Yes: SHA-256 aliases | integrity status in the case record (`DUPLICATE_CONTENT`) |
| Suitability | Yes: admission state | `modality_admission`, `quality_state`, `queue_state` |

: Coverage dimensions and where they come from. {#tbl-coverage tbl-colwidths="[26,40,34]"}

The full sampling policy, including planning targets and open owner decisions, is in the *Team Image Sampling Requirements*. Its register (`docs/clinician/sampling/REQUIREMENTS_TRACEABILITY.md`) marks which items are software-enforced.
